newsitem.title: USA: Fairfax County, Va., to seek $500 mln school GOs.
newsitem.headline: Fairfax County, Va., to seek $500 mln school GOs.

text.p: Virginia's Fairfax County Board of Supervisors has endorsed a five-year building plan that calls for two general obligation bond issues totalling up to $500 million, school officials said Wednesday.
"We plan to go to referendum this November for a $225 to $250 million package," said Roger Webb, assistant superintendent for facilities services.

The county school board was scheduled to fine-tune the building list at an April 24 meeting and then vote on a final proposal on May 27. The Board of Supervisors would then have to approve it before it could be placed on the ballot.
A referendum for a second, similarly-sized issue is planned for November 1999, Webb said.
Voters approved the county's last school bond issue of $204 million in 1995.
"We go like clockwork every two to three years for a referendum," Webb said. "That's been our pattern for 20 years or more. It's worked very well for us."
Voters did reject school bonds in the mid-1970s, but have approved several since.
"We've developed the credibility. There's a known need for schools in Fairfax County and people value their schools," Webb said.
The county's student population has grown by more than 3,000 a year. The five-year building plan calls for construcion of six new schools and renovation and expansion at 60 others.

The school district has no independent taxing authority, so its bonds are issued by Fairfax County. Its general obligation bonds are rated a top-flight Aaa by Moody's Investors Service Inc and Standard & Poor's Corp.
